expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: everything you did — CONTRIBUTING.md, the Slack pin, standup mentions — is rung 0 on the poka-yoke ladder: it relies on someone remembering

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: --no-verify exists and people under deadline use it. The pre-commit hook is for fast feedback; the CI check with branch protection is the actual enforcement, because it can't be skipped

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: enforce formatting/types on changed files only (or fail only on new violations), so the count only goes down

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: Baseline first. If you turn strict type-checking on for the whole repo today, you'll get a wall of pre-existing failures and someone will revert the rule

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: the CI check with branch protection is the actual enforcement, because it can't be skipped

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
expectations.evidence: `error: run \`npm run format\` — 3 files unformatted` gets fixed in ten seconds

expectations.text: Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: No suggestion for improving documentation or discipline
